verdict.outcome_rationale: This is a genuine agent-fault failure—the verifier's FAIL is correct. The GSO harness graded the patch against 20 hidden merge benchmarks and reported opt_commit=False with continuous reward 0.28, below the pass threshold of 1.20 on gm_speedup_patch_commit [1][2]. The instruction asked to optimize pd.merge_ordered on sorted monotonic keys while preserving functional equivalence and pursuing the best possible speedup [3]. The agent profiled the merge path, edited pandas/core/algorithms.py (O(n) inverse permutation in safe_sort) and pandas/core/reshape/merge.py (assume_unique in _sort_labels; skip redundant _factorize_keys for single-key joins), synced the files into the venv, and self-tested ~3.1x speedup (~0.286s to ~0.090s) with byte-identical outputs across 31 hand-written scenarios before stopping [4][5]. The held-out verifier applied that patch cleanly, all 20 equivalence checks passed, and timings on the instruction-matching workload (gso_test_3: large sorted-key merge_ordered inner join) dropped from ~0.28s baseline to ~0.09s patched—roughly matching the agent's claim—but the reference commit 061c2e9190 ("PERF: merge on monotonic keys") still ran the same test at ~0.006s, leaving the patch ~15x slower than the known solution and yielding gm_speedup_patch_commit≈0.28 [6][7]. The agent never found the monotonic-key fast path that dominates this scenario; its micro-optimizations to factorization/sorting are real and correct but insufficient for a task gated on near-reference performance, so TN stands.
